rule: When killing a process, target it by PID (identified via ps first), never pkill/killall by name pattern, since pattern matches can kill unrelated processes including the caller's own shell.
check: PreToolUse-hook regex-matching the Bash command string for literal `pkill` or `killall` invocations and blocking/warning
misses: functionally equivalent name-based kills that avoid the literal tokens, e.g. `kill $(pgrep -f name)`, `for pid in $(ps aux|grep name|awk ...); do kill $pid; done`, or xargs-based kill loops

rule: Deployed/cluster state must always trace to committed, pushed manifests: never build or deploy from a dirty or unpushed tree, and never land a build-input change without the corresponding image build and pin bump landing together.
check: CI-job/CronJob (aifleet manifest-drift CronJob, fd deploy-pin-check) diffing live cluster state against the committed manifest, plus a pre-build check (`git status --porcelain` / branch-ahead-of-remote check) before `docker build`/`kubectl apply`
misses: the 2026-07-30 recurrence shapes: a clean-but-unpushed local commit (declared state of record still stale on the remote ref) and a Dockerfile change landed on main without triggering the corresponding image build — both require correlating build provenance and remote ref state, not just a local dirty-tree check

rule: The agent may write/edit the live MEMORY.md index and individual memory files directly without founder authorization each time; everything else the protected-path guard covers (settings.json, global CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md file itself, hooks, .ssh, credentials) remains blocked.
check: protected-path-write-guard.sh PreToolUse hook allowlist, which was edited to exempt the live memory-index path while still denying Write/Edit/Bash writes to the other protected paths

rule: Route memory content to the right tier — project-specific rules into that repo's CLAUDE.md, cross-cutting coordinator behavior and the safety kernel stay in global MEMORY.md — and verify a memory is already preserved in engram before archiving its flat file.
Every session must fan out to multiple agents rather than a single lane, and every spawned agent must run on an efficient/cheap pinned tier rather than defaulting to expensive Fable execution.

Every agent() call inside a Workflow script (and every Agent-tool subagent spawned for execution) must pin an explicit non-Fable model (opus/sonnet/haiku); omitting the model field silently inherits the session model, which on a Fable session makes the executor Fable.
check: A schema/static check on the Workflow script's tool-call input requiring every agent(...) call to include a non-null, non-default `model` field before the Workflow is allowed to execute
misses: whether the pinned model is actually the CHEAPEST tier capable of the task (over-tiering) — that requires judging task difficulty — and standalone Agent-tool spawns made outside a Workflow script that a script-level check would not inspect

rule: A session may not approve/merge its own self-authored, self-orchestrated PR unless the work is covered by a founder-approved plan (plan approval counts as merge authorization) or a different agent adversarially verified it; verification claims must be backed by a linked, fetched artifact, not just asserted.
check: PreToolUse-hook on `gh pr merge`/`gh pr review` comparing the PR's author identity (`gh pr view --json author`) to the current session's git/gh identity and blocking a match unless an override/exception flag is present
misses: whether a founder-approved plan actually covers the specific work (the exception path), whether a cited CI/verification artifact's CONTENT genuinely supports the claim rather than just existing, and whether the 'different agent adversarially verified' condition was truly independent — all require reading and judging content, not just author metadata

rule: For actions already within the authorized envelope (reversible, precedented, invariant-guarded), the agent must decide and execute, reporting outcomes rather than narrating pending/conditional futures or offering veto windows.

Published writing should candidly include the team's own mistakes and failure-ledger material as a differentiator, while excluding proprietary/security specifics, internal topology, client names, and retracted statistics presented as live facts.

Do not activate full, context-heavy persona agent files (14-16KB roster definitions) without explicit founder reason; default to anonymous agent types with a distilled 10-15 line role charter instead, and keep personality (work habits) separate from writing-function/voice.
check: A lint/hook checking the spawned agent-type file referenced in an Agent/Task spawn against a known list of full persona files (or a file-size threshold) and flagging spawns that reference one
misses: whether an explicit founder reason was actually given for activating the persona (a semantic judgment) and whether a supposedly 'distilled charter' has drifted back into carrying voice/personality content that belongs to a writing-function spec instead

rule: Writes to the plans directory (and generally, background-session writes) must never be blocked by the worktree-isolation guard; this was implemented by setting worktree.bgIsolation to 'none' in ~/.claude/settings.json, which disables the bg-isolation guard entirely rather than just for plan paths.
check: worktree.bgIsolation setting value ('none') in ~/.claude/settings.json, which governs whether the bg-isolation guard fires on background Write/Edit calls

rule: Operational learnings (runbook steps, gotchas, drift findings, deploy patterns) produced in a session must be written into the owning repo's project-level docs (CLAUDE.md/DESIGN.md) in the same turn they are proven, not left only in session memory.

Once the founder has authorized force-pushing a specific session-owned branch for a specific bounded task, the agent should not re-ask for each subsequent force-push of that same branch within that task, but must re-ask if branch ownership becomes ambiguous, the target branch changes, or a genuinely new task begins.
